aner_65.name: Aner
aner_65.what: A Levitical town in the western half-tribe of Manasseh, given to the Kohathite clans.
aner_65.today: Exact site unknown; possibly the same as Taanach in northern Israel.
key: From the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner and Bileam went to the remaining Kohathite clans (1 Chronicles 6).
Joshua's parallel list names Taanach and Gath-rimmon from western Manasseh instead (Joshua 21).

beer_165.name: Beer
beer_165.what: A place where Jotham fled after proclaiming his fable against his brother Abimelech.
key: From Mount Gerizim Jotham told his parable of the trees against Abimelech and Shechem (Judges 9).
He then fled to Beer and lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech (Judges 9).

bene-jaakan_174.name: Bene-jaakan
bene-jaakan_174.what: A wilderness campsite of Israel, also called the wells of the Bene-jaakan, near Moserah.
bene-jaakan_174.today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness south of Canaan.
key: Israel set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan (Numbers 33).
From Bene-jaakan they moved on and camped at Hor-haggidgad (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled Israel journeying from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died (Deuteronomy 10).

elkosh_371.name: Elkosh
elkosh_371.what: The hometown of the prophet Nahum, who is called the Elkoshite.
key: The book of Nahum is the vision of Nahum of Elkosh concerning Nineveh (Nahum 1).
Nahum announced that the LORD would make a complete end of Nineveh (Nahum 1).

erech_407.name: Erech
erech_407.what: An ancient city in the land of Shinar, among the first cities of Nimrod's kingdom.
key: Nimrod's kingdom began with Babel, Erech, and Accad in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10).
Men of Erech were among the peoples settled in Samaria who wrote against Jerusalem's rebuilding (Ezra 4).

harod_529.name: Harod
harod_529.what: A spring near Mount Gilboa where Gideon camped; two of David's mighty men were called men of Harod.
harod_529.today: Likely Ain Jalud at the foot of Mount Gilboa, northern Israel.
key: Gideon and his army camped beside the spring of Harod, with Midian's camp to the north (Judges 7).
There the LORD reduced Gideon's army, sending home the fearful and testing the rest at the water (Judges 7).
Shammah of Harod and Elika of Harod are listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).

mesha_787.name: Mesha
mesha_787.what: A place marking one end of the territory where the descendants of Joktan lived.
mesha_787.today: Exact site unknown; possibly in Arabia.
key: Joktan's sons lived from Mesha in the direction of Sephar, the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).
Joktan, a descendant of Shem through Eber, had thirteen sons, including Sheba, Ophir, and Havilah (Genesis 10).

moresheth_819.name: Moresheth
moresheth_819.what: A town in Judah's lowland, the hometown of the prophet Micah.
moresheth_819.today: Likely Tell el-Judeideh, near Beit Guvrin in the Shephelah, Israel.
key: The word of the LORD came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah (Micah 1).
In his lament over Judah's towns, Micah named Moresheth-gath (Micah 1).
Elders recalled Micah of Moresheth, whose warning moved Hezekiah to seek the LORD (Jeremiah 26).

nehelam_886.name: Nehelam
nehelam_886.what: The home or family of Shemaiah, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
key: The LORD gave Jeremiah a message for Shemaiah of Nehelam among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).
Shemaiah had written to the priest Zephaniah, urging him to confine Jeremiah (Jeremiah 29).
The LORD said Shemaiah prophesied unsent and would have no descendant among the people (Jeremiah 29).

shamir_1061.name: Shamir
shamir_1061.what: A town in the hill country of Ephraim where the judge Tola lived and was buried.
key: Tola son of Puah, a man of Issachar, lived at Shamir in Ephraim's hill country (Judges 10).
After judging Israel twenty-three years, Tola died and was buried at Shamir (Judges 10).

gate_of_the_valley_1195.name: Valley Gate
gate_of_the_valley_1195.what: A gate in Jerusalem's wall facing a valley, used by Nehemiah for his night inspection of the walls.
gate_of_the_valley_1195.today: Possibly on the southwest side of the City of David, Jerusalem.
key: King Uzziah built fortified towers in Jerusalem at the Valley Gate (2 Chronicles 26).
Nehemiah went out by night through the Valley Gate to inspect the broken walls (Nehemiah 2).
Hanun and the people of Zanoah rebuilt it and set its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
